title.narrative: ENVELOPE 1: Reduce the spread of Cholera by enchanting access for safe, clean and sustainable WASH services in targeted locations

description.narrative:
UNICEF aims to respond to the most vulnerable population in the cholera hot-spot sub-districts with safe and adequate WASH services. The project intends to curb the spread of cholera with proposed actions in line with the ICCG Syria/AWD Cholera Response Plan and Winterization Plan. The number of people targeted in this project is 233,672 (composing of 44,398 men 49,072 women 67,765 boys 72,437 girls 60,517 PWDs) living in the host communities, informal settlement and camps in Aleppo and Idleb Governorates. The proposed intervention can be summarized as following:
I) Carryout rehabilitation, maintenance and operation of water stations and distribution networks in the sub-district of Ariha (Idleb governorate) to ensure the affected population in targeted communities have access to safe and adequate drinking water for 19,908 vulnerable people (3,782 men 4,181 women 5,773 boys 6,172 girls 6,230 PWDs).
II) Carryout rehabilitation and maintenance for the sanitation infrastructure in the sub-districts of Azaz and Al Bab (Aleppo governorates) to improve wastewater disposal of vulnerable communities during winter and flood for 206,264 (39,191 men, 43,316 women, 59,817 boys, 63,940 girls 54,187 PWDs) – the services will also support potential outbreaks of AWD/cholera and reduce potential blockage of septic tanks during winter.
III) Carryout door-to-door cholera risk communication and distribute cholera kits (that contains soaps, jerry-cans, Aquatabs and printed preventive messages) within 70% targeted population in the project proposal which is 233,672 people in coordination with Health and WASH clusters, in and around affected households.
IV) Carryout Rehabilitation for WASH Facilities in two Health Care Facilities which will serve at least 7,500 patients (1,425 men 1,575 women 2,175 boys 2,325 girls 100 PWD ).
V) Implement RCCE (hygiene promotion sessions with cholera prevention objective) including use of videos, posters, banners along with trainings for field facilitators for the active NGOs as a part of RCCE plan for Cholera and AWD, targeting 233,672 (composing of 44,398 men 49,072 women 71,888 boys 72,437 girls 60,517 PWDs) people.
